1. Plausibility. A faithful same-topic proof is mathematically plausible, but it is not presently supported by a known literature construction. The unrestricted all-DMG greatest-representative statement is precisely beyond the proved E-separation results and is stated as conjectural in the direct E source. Mogensen–Hansen’s potential-parent/potential-sibling closure cannot be imported: it concerns one homogeneous μ-separation model, whereas E-separation is read in a target-dependent two-copy lift with conditioning set D(B,C). Thus completing thm:single-edge-transfer would amount to supplying a genuinely new marked, copy-aware replacement theorem.

2. Next exact construction to attempt. Do not try another unmarked potential-edge predicate. Prove the following occurrence-local lemma first.

Marked contextual replacement lemma. Fix an E-query q=(A,B,C), write L_q(X)=Lift_{B,C}(X), and let G≡_E H. Let e∈E(H)\E(G). Suppose a shortest D(B,C)-open route π in L_q(G+e) witnessing A not-perp_E B | C uses a lifted occurrence e-tilde. Put π=α e-tilde β, choosing a shortest witness so that the chosen occurrence is unique. Then there are routes α_H,β_H in L_q(H), not using e-tilde, whose boundary interfaces agree with those of α,β in all of: the exact endpoint copies at both ends of e-tilde; the incidence mark contributed by the adjacent route edge at each boundary; membership of each boundary state in D(B,C); and, when a boundary becomes a collider after insertion of e-tilde, the required directed-ancestry-to-D(B,C) certificate. Consequently α_H e-tilde β_H is D(B,C)-open in L_q(H).

If this lemma holds, thm:single-edge-transfer is immediate by contradiction: assume A perp_E^G B | C but A not-perp_E^{G+e} B | C; contextual replacement constructs the same dependence in H, contradicting G≡_E H.

The proof attempt should be organized as follows. First prove a shortest-witness normal form: a profile-changing lifted edge occurrence can be selected uniquely, and the two residual pieces are edge-e-free. Do not silently assume ordinary path simplification preserves collider activation; prove it for the actual lifted openness definition. Then enumerate boundary signatures directly from the Lift incidence table. Split first by (1) an SCC-changing directed edge and (2) the first bidirected edge outside an occupied SCC rectangle. Within each case split by the actual copy pair of e-tilde and by the four adjacent-mark patterns at its two boundaries. For every collider boundary, retain the particular ancestry witness into D(B,C); “the endpoint is an ancestor of some conditioned vertex” without the copy and target information is insufficient.

For each resulting signature, construct an E-query probe whose dependence is equivalent to realization of that marked prefix or suffix in the same lift L_q. Equality of E-models may then transfer that probe from G to H. The decisive sublemma is: Marked-probe completeness. Every boundary signature occurring in the above shortest-witness normal form is observable by finitely many ordinary E-separation statements while holding B,C, hence D(B,C), fixed. This is the simplest non-circular reduction left: it identifies exactly the extra fact needed to splice around missing G-edges in H. Before attempting all cases, test marked-probe completeness on the SCC-changing-arrow case with one fixed copy pair. If even one required tail/head or ancestry signature is not observable through ordinary E-queries, the replacement program fails under the present assumptions.

3. Invalid routes to avoid. Do not infer endpoint marks, copy indices, ancestry, or SCC-tail certificates merely from equality of the unmarked E-independence models. Do not apply Mogensen–Hansen Lemmas 5.4/5.8 or Theorem 5.9 directly, or intersect their potential-parent/sibling predicates over targets. The target-dependent lifts are different graphs/models, and E-equivalence does not establish the full μ-equivalence hypotheses those results require. Do not splice the G-prefix and G-suffix directly around e in H; H may omit either piece. Do not let the transferred replacement itself use e unless a separate route-reduction lemma proves that the resulting repetition can be eliminated while preserving copy states, marks, and collider activation. Do not use finite exhaustive checks as a proof. Do not invoke antitonicity through an unrestricted Gamma(G) before proving Gamma(G)≡_E G; that is the desired conclusion in another form.

4. Headline disposition. Unless marked-probe completeness and the contextual replacement lemma are actually proved, the unconditional unrestricted-DMG headline must be adjusted under the same assumptions. The defensible headline is the proved fixed-profile/occupied-rectangle greatest-completion theorem, with unrestricted union closure stated conditionally on thm:single-edge-transfer (or explicitly as the open conjectural extension). Retaining the unconditional headline without this lemma would claim a resolution of the direct source’s all-DMG conjecture, not a literature-backed completion.
